def attach_particle(word: str, particle: str) -> str:
    # Digit to Sino-Korean pronunciation (what batchim it has)
    # True = has batchim (consonant), False = no batchim (vowel)
    digit_batchim = {
        '0': True,   # 영
        '1': True,   # 일
        '2': False,  # 이
        '3': True,   # 삼
        '4': False,  # 사
        '5': False,  # 오
        '6': True,   # 육
        '7': True,   # 칠
        '8': True,   # 팔
        '9': False,  # 구
    }
    
    last_char = word[-1]
    
    # Check if last character is a digit
    if last_char.isdigit():
        has_batchim = digit_batchim[last_char]
    else:
        # Check if it's a Hangul syllable
        char_code = ord(last_char)
        if 0xAC00 <= char_code <= 0xD7A3:
            # Hangul syllable
            # Each syllable = (initial × 588) + (medial × 28) + final
            relative_code = char_code - 0xAC00
            final_index = relative_code % 28
            has_batchim = final_index != 0
            
            # Special case for 으로/로: if particle is 으로/로 and final is ㄹ
            if particle == "으로/로" and final_index == 8:  # ㄹ is at index 8
                has_batchim = False
        else:
            # Not a Hangul character, assume no batchim
            has_batchim = False
    
    # Select the appropriate form
    forms = particle.split('/')
    if has_batchim:
        return word + forms[0]
    else:
        return word + forms[1]
